content.value_statement: Writing a technical survival chapter can lose emotional tension or clear choices. This skill provides a structured roleplay scene for building a signal tower and deciding what its message reveals.
actual_capabilities: Sets a roleplay scene where Stella evaluates a damaged long-range communication system.
Guides resource collection and improvised construction using fictional crystals and salvaged equipment.
Provides dialogue beats for a signal transmission and an ethical disclosure decision.
Offers branches for an Earth response or an unknown local signal.
Connects the chapter to future escape, alien encounter, ruins, and settlement storylines.
limitations: It is a writing prompt, not engineering guidance for real communication equipment.
The scientific concepts are fictional and intentionally simplified for storytelling.
It does not generate a complete novel or manage continuity outside the supplied chapter.
Players must choose the final branch and supply their own responses during roleplay.

use_cases.title: Continue a survival campaign
use_cases.description: Run a focused chapter in which a stranded engineer tries to contact home after a crash.

use_cases.title: Design a science-fiction scene
use_cases.description: Use the staged beats to draft a story scene balancing technical work, hope, and ethical uncertainty.

use_cases.title: Plan branching narrative content
use_cases.description: Adapt the two response routes into a larger campaign with clear hooks for later chapters.

prompt_templates.title: Start the chapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Repairing Signal Tower. Start with Stella assessing the damaged communication panel. Ask me whether she should begin the repair.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on engineering
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the resource and construction stages. Keep the technical language simple and show one unexpected power problem before the tower works.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the message
prompt_templates.prompt: Play the signal transmission stage. Present Stella with a clear choice between reporting only survival facts and revealing Gaia discoveries.

prompt_templates.title: Build a campaign branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Repairing Signal Tower to create two distinct outcomes: a weak Earth reply and a mysterious Gaia signal. End each route with a hook for the next chapter.

output_examples.input: Start the signal tower repair scene.
output: Stella studies the damaged panel and lists the missing antenna, amplifier, and power components.
She asks whether the risk of rebuilding the system is worth the chance to contact Earth.

output_examples.input: Give me the mysterious response route.
output: After several days without an Earth reply, the scanner receives rhythmic patterns from thirty kilometers away.
Stella realizes an unknown intelligence may have heard her transmission and asks whether to investigate.

output_examples.input: Help Stella decide what to send.
output_examples.output: The scene frames a choice between a short survival report and a fuller message about Gaia, its ruins, and its intelligent creatures.

best_practices: Choose a response branch before continuing so the chapter has a clear direction.
Keep Stella’s technical confidence balanced with practical setbacks and emotional uncertainty.
Use the disclosure decision to connect player choices to later story consequences.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the fictional engineering details as instructions for real equipment.
Do not resolve every problem immediately because setbacks create narrative tension.
Do not force a single ending when player choice is central to the chapter.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It guides a roleplay or writing chapter about repairing a signal tower on a fictional planet.

faq.question: Is this real engineering advice?
faq.answer: No. The equipment, crystals, and scientific details support fiction only.

faq.question: Can I choose the ending?
faq.answer: Yes. You can pursue an Earth response, a mysterious local response, or a failed repair that changes Stella’s outlook.

faq.question: Who is Stella?
faq.answer: Stella Chen is the stranded engineer and central character of the chapter.

faq.question: Can I use this for a game campaign?
faq.answer: Yes. The branches include hooks for escape, alien encounter, ancient ruins, and settlement chapters.

faq.question: Does the skill write the entire story?
faq.answer: No. It supplies a structured scene and dialogue direction for an interactive continuation.
